this waterfall is a hour or so drive from the city of malang it seems to be in the middle of nowhere but there are many small shops and eateries warungs at the parkinglot next to the entrance so it isn t uninhabited here all toilets come with a charge even if you seem to be the customer of the place that owns the toilet to got to the waterfall is subject to an entrance fee after it you will walk on a concrete path to a viewpoint where you see the semi circular opening where the water comes down it is an impressive view and you can use two levels and a small plattform for taking pictures of people and the fall here you don t see the bottom of the fall after that you will have to go back a few steps to reach the place where the concrete path starts taking you down to the bottom of the fall most of this path is steep and only sometimes with something to hold on to there are sections with metal steps or metal grids to walk on and those are often more slippery than the concrete or the rocks you will have to walk through flowing water so your shoes need to agree with that there are small areas where you can take a rest and you will pass at least one section where drinks etc are sold at the bottom you will walk back and forth over log bridges that cross an active stream there will be mist coming towards you in this area that mist is similar to a light rain and it gets stronger the closer you get to the bottom of the fall here you ll probably appreciate a rain cape if you have one you will need around minutes to get to the viewpoint and all the way down to the mist at the bottom and something similar to get back up to the parking lot another half an hour is enough for looking around at the bottom the viewpoint works for most visitors but going to the bottom is definitely not for everyone most people use shorts t shirt and sandals or flip flops for this visit there are people renting out shoes to those that don t have any there are cameras checking what happens on the trail down but please be careful if you go down

originally en route to teluk asmara we were redirected by a local driver to pantai tiga warna a hidden gem tucked within a conservation area access is limited to preserve the ecosystem so advance reservation is highly recommended we chanced a walk in and were fortunate upon arrival staff conduct an availability check followed by a brief orientation visitors are then transported via trike to another checkpoint where belongings are inspected to ensure no littering items are rechecked upon return a certified local guide is mandatory though costs are more economical if shared among a group our guide offered a boat ride to shorten the trek though this depends on tidal conditions the journey is not for the faint hearted passing through eerie submerged mangrove areas that eerily conjure thoughts of crocodiles however the effort is well worth it pantai tiga warna reveals a pristine beach with vibrant snorkeling opportunities for those who choose to hike back a visit to nearby gatra beach facing teluk asmara makes for a scenic finale that said the terrain is demanding and i would advise against this trip for the elderly or those not in good physical condition

i was originally hesitant to hire a horse when i was approached by a few horse owners as soon as we parked the jeep but i followed along halfheartedly because everyone else in my group wanted to it turned out to be a lifesaver the walk to the crater is quite far and the sand is thick everywhere especially near the stairs where it gets deep and powdery it was hot and there were horse droppings here and there so i was comfortable enough riding on a horse instead of walking through that it was my first time ever riding a horse and it didnt disappoint some horses were quite colorful with their bright gear and saddles the owner walked the horse for me all the way to the crater stairs the cost was idr k along the way i noticed locals selling food and drinks but it was near the stairs area where i saw them selling edelweiss flowers in colors like purple red and blue when i reached the stairs i was glad they had two lanesone for climbing and one for descendingso we didnt bump into each other there are even rest areas on both sides where you can stop without blocking others reaching the top was fantastic standing on the mouth of bromo looking down into the craters opening and hearing the giant furnace sound it produces was a humbling experience after some time i went down and the horse owner was there to save my life again for the ride back i dont think i could identify him because all the owners wear almost identical clothes and masks but i was glad he remembered me and found me in the middle of the crowd what initially felt like an unnecessary expense was something i ended up paying for more willingly

tucked away in the remote southern coast of banyuwangi green bay teluk hijau in sarongan village is a breathtaking hidden paradise that showcases natures artistry through its unique geological formations and stunning coastal landscape the bay gets its name from the mesmerizing emeraldgreen waters that contrast dramatically with the towering limestone cliffs surrounding the cove creating a scene that looks more like a tropical fjord than a typical javanese beach geologically green bay is fascinating the steep cliffs reveal layers of sedimentary rock formations that tell a story of ancient seabeds uplifted by tectonic activity while the bay itself was carved out by relentless wave action over millennia the beach consists of smooth pebbles and coarse greenish sand a result of the weathering of olivinerich rocks in the area which contributes to the waters distinctive greenish hue when sunlight hits the mineral particles suspended in the clear waters during low tide fascinating tidal pools form among the wavecut platforms revealing tiny marine ecosystems perfect for exploration accessing green bay requires some adventure spirit as visitors must descend a steep winding path through lush coastal vegetation but the effort is rewarded with one of javas most spectacular coastal views the bays unique microclimate creates interesting weather patterns with mist often clinging to the cliffs in the morning adding to the mystical atmosphere what makes green bay particularly special is its untouched quality there are no resorts or restaurants just pure unspoiled nature the waters are exceptionally clear allowing visibility of colorful fish and coral formations making it excellent for snorkeling when the waves are calm nearby a small waterfall cascades directly onto the beach its freshwater stream mixing with the ocean in a fascinating display of natures hydrological processes the surrounding area features several sea caves and interesting rock formations that beg to be explored though visitors should exercise caution during high tide when some areas become inaccessible the journey to green bay takes you through beautiful rural landscapes of banyuwangis southern coast passing traditional villages and offering glimpses of local life far from tourist trails while facilities are minimal visitors should bring their own food and water this very lack of development preserves the bays magical untouched atmosphere the best time to visit is during the dry season when the sea is calmer and the green color of the water is most vibrant for geology enthusiasts nature lovers or anyone seeking one of javas last truly pristine coastal wonders green bay offers an unforgettable experience where powerful geological forces have created a landscape of breathtaking beauty the interplay of light on the water throughout the day creates an everchanging palette of blues and greens while the sound of waves echoing off the cliffs provides a natural symphony a perfect reminder of natures ability to create masterpieces when left undisturbed

pasir bisik which translates to whispering sands is a wellknown sandy area located within the caldera of mount bromo in east java indonesia it covers an expansive area of over hectares on the eastern side of the crater the name pasir bisik became popular around largely due to the indonesian film pasir bisik whispering sands directed by nan achnas and starring dian sastrowardoyo and christine hakim the film tells the story of a village girl named daya who often lies on the sands and hears whispers from the moving sand which inspired the poetic name for this area in the management of bromo tengger meru national park decided to remove the name pasir bisik along with several other tourist spot names reverting to the original local names as part of an effort to preserve the cultural heritage and natural environment of the area

balur is a great park for wildlife watching or birding with many beautiful landscapes i do a lot of wildlife watching and photography around the world and i thought overall this park is top notch it might just require a little more effort and careful timing if wildlife is your goal i visited for days in early oct i stayed near the park and drove a rented scooter in every day here are some things the park is great for and some drawbacks landscapes there is a good diversity of landscapes within the park on the drive in you see a lot of tropical dry forest with some wettergreener forests deeper within the park there is also the very dry and open savannah region and a lot of mangroves and forest near the beach there is really just one road through the park to the beach and not much opportunity for hiking so if your primary focus is seeing the landscape you could see everything in one day wildlife you can see lots of green peacocks wild buffalo deer langur monkeys wild pigs and hornbills near bama beach but timing matters a lot if you are interested in seeing wildlife you should either go by yourself like i did or do a tour that visits the park in the evening i spent all day in the park and i can tell you that if you are on a tour that goes through the park any time from ampm you arent going to see much in terms of wildlife because its too hot and the animals are in the forests where its cooler as soon as it starts to cool down you will see loads of deer peacocks and other animals emerge onto the savannah and start crossing the roads in other areas my biggest complaint about this park is that it opens too late in the morning unfortunately the park doesnt open until am which means by the time you get your entry ticket and drive into the park its already getting hot and youve really missed the best wildlife watching period of the day you will still be able to catch the tail end of the morning period and you can see a lot in the evening but for a wildlifefocused park its frustrating that they dont let people into the park earlier most of the wildlifefocused parks ive visited in north america or africa open much earlier because they understand that this is primetime for wildlife again you can see a lot of great wildlife in the park but if you want to see wildlife and you are taking a tour from banyuwangi make sure the tour doesnt leave the park too early in the day otherwise you will likely be disappointed i expected to see a lot of banteng in the park based on the photos and reviews i saw online but i did not see any despite being in the park all day for days this may be a seasonal thing but just be aware they arent easy to see unlike the wild buffalo which always seem to be around i never really expect to see big cats like leopards in any park but i talked to some of the workers in the park and they said they do see them quite frequently unfortunately they only see them at night crossing the road and as a tourist you cant be in the park at night nice to know the leopards are there though even if your chances of actually seeing them is very small i also feel the park could use some investment the mangrove trail is closed the observation tower at the savannah is closed and overall there arent a lot of hiking opportunities there used to be lodging inside the park but this is also closed bama beach is the center of activity its much cooler during the day and very pretty the facilities are also much better there with some small restaurants and decent bathrooms overall balur was one of my favorite spots in indonesia there is amazing wildlife if you visit at the right time and the open savannah with balur mountain in the background is beautiful

this stop was part of our organized tour package for a mt bromo sunrise and hiking through the seas of sands to the top of mt bromo crater our driver dropped us off at the parking area at am and from there it is a steep climb to the viewpoint the path has a mixture of cement road dirt and rocky road and stairs the sunrise during our particular visit was blocked by clouds on the horizon common in march as its the end of rainy season but it was still a spectacular reveal of the smoking mt bromo mt batok and mt meru highest peak in java with the daylight it is awe inspiring to contemplate being at the edge of the collapsed massive ancient tengger volcano it seems we got lucky with being able to see anything at all because the previous few days had cloud cover throughout the caldera throughout sunrise we got super lucky to catch a small eruption from mt meru the walk down was also offered stunning views of the surrounding area overall remarkable and well worth the early wake up to experience practical considerations safety items to be aware of there are a lot of other vehicles so be aware of them as they may not see you we did witness an accident and it was horrific the hike had very few lights so a headlamp or torchflashlight would be incredibly useful look out for horse droppingspoop especially on the way down as it could lead to a nasty slipfall during our visit the upper level of the viewpoint did not have a railing behind the bench and someone could literally walk off in the dark timing we happened to book during the eid holiday and it was crowded potentially equivalent to peak season so coming early to find a spot is helpful but be kind and ready to share the view with others further back comfort if its windy it could feel quite cold so consider dressing in layers there are also limited restrooms on the path up that are idr there is supposedly a way to climb further up king kong hill but it looked very steep with loose rock it could have been challenging climbing up in the dark without a guide with a difficult to see trail thats overgrown but for us with just sneakers instead of hiking boots and no hiking poles it didnt seem safely doable to come back down

i visited madakaripura in december reaching the falls around pm the trip started with a mute ojek ride from the parking area the road is clean and lined with green trees at the trailhead our guide mr timo provided helmets there are toilets near the local stalls where ladies sell forest honey they mentioned which bottle sizes are allowed on planes and i promised to buy some on the way back the trail is easy but involves several river crossings the stones are slippery so you have to pay attention mr timo helped us across one by one eventually you reach a point where you need a raincoat to walk under the overhanging cliffs water falls from the rocks above like a curtain soaking everything my group took photos on the boulders here i walked further toward the main waterfall which is located inside a large halfopen hole mr timo told me that this place is named after gajah mada a famous prime mister and military leader of the majapahit empire this is where he was last known to meditate and disappear i managed to get near but i wasnt allowed to go inside for safety reasons the scale of the canyon it feels like a great craft of the divinea sight you dont see just anywhere i think reaching this place in the afternoon made photography difficult the lighting was low and the constant water spray made it hard to get a clear shot we were also hurried to leave because the guide said it was going to rain the whole trip took about hours i went back with the honey

we visited pantai srau on the th day of eid with a group of people traveling in a hiace the parking was easy and spacious which is a big plus when you re coming in a larger vehicle or with family the beach itself is pretty and stretches quite long offering some great views and even a spot to catch the sunset if you stay late enough entrance fee was also very reasonable at rp k per person plus rp k for the car around the beach area there are plenty of food options from small warung style eateries to a few that market themselves as restaurants unfortunately we made the mistake of choosing the virgin pantai srau restaurant and it turned out to be the worst part of the visit most of their menu was sold out the service was slow and unhelpful and they still charged more than the warungs despite only offering things like spicy nasi goreng and instant noodles indomie overall pantai srau is a lovely beach with easy access good photo spots and fair entry prices but if you re hungry skip the fancy looking places and just eat at the warungs for better value and faster service

i visited in december from the parking area with the bromo crater directly in front of us our jeep turned left skirting the black and whitish foot of the mountain until the landscape opened up into green hills the area is covered in fresh green ferns that look like a never ending landscape it was a hot morning as it got warmer i took off my outer sweater leaving me covered with my light spf windbreaker i was glad i had my sunglasses and cap i heard the high pitched chipmunk style music first and then i felt the funfair vibe i still have that atok ooo atok sound stuck in my head i saw many other people who were so determined to take photos with the green ferns even though the sun was intense i wanted to walk deeper into the ferns myself they look so bushy fresh and green but i was sweating and felt like my face skin was burning so i stayed back after taking photos we sat under a seller s big umbrella on portable chairs our guide mr kiki was very kind and bought us two skewers of aci cor with two different sauces he said he wanted us to experience the local foods i was moved by this i ve never had a guide buy food for me before and it really changed my perspective as it got warmer and we were running out of time we had to leave the fern garden further up was the teletubbies hills area i quietly regretted that we didn t manage to visit that specific spot but sitting in the shade eating and chatting with a great guide was still a highlight next time i come here i would like to find mr kiki again

a meaningful historical museum visiting the karno museum was truly an unforgettable and meaningful experience located in blitar east java this museum holds a deep historical value as it preserves the life journey of indonesias first president ir soekarno the place is clean wellorganized and full of stories that bring the nations past to life walking through the exhibition rooms i could see various personal belongings that karno once usedhis clothes books furniture and even handwritten notes these items made the visit feel so real and emotional as if i was stepping back in time to witness his struggle and passion for indonesias independence the museums atmosphere is calm and respectful allowing visitors to truly reflect on karnos legacy the displays are informative and beautifully arranged guiding visitors through different stages of his lifefrom his exile in ende to his powerful speeches as the nations leader the staff were also very friendly and knowledgeable adding warmth to the historical environment for me the most fascinating part was the painting that seems to beat like a heartits so unique and gives a symbolic meaning of karnos everlasting spirit overall the karno museum is not just a place to learn history but also a reminder of indonesias struggle and unity its definitely worth visiting and a mustsee destination when youre in blitar

one of the most beautiful places i have ever been to the view is breathtaking and the trek was challenging and exhausting we started our hike through sumber brantas you would need a health certificate from a government clinic to be able to climb not sure if they scrutimize it though as we were not this is transportation available from basecamp upto the base of the mountain which makes the climb easier the view on the way is also amazing from there on its climbclimbclimb there are three checkpoints until you reach the camp site the trek from up till is the most difficult and the journey would take up about hours from the base of the mountain the view near the camp ground is amazing and definitely worth the tiring climb from here you could climb summits arjuno which is to hours one way kembar and weiliriang that takes about in total back to camp and finally kembar there is not a lot of wildlife that you will come across other than some birds and wild boars that would come to camp at night in search of food there are also panthers that you might come across accoding to the rangers at basecamp our friends got a glimpse of one there have been no attacks at all and is not something to worry about its recommended that a minumum of people climb together unless you have a guide and a porter which can also be arranged at basecamp finally you need to carry a lot of water as it will be a to day affair and there are no close water sources near camp the nearest water source is and half hour away

i visited in december from the parking area with the bromo crater directly in front of us our jeep turned left skirting the black and whitish foot of the mountain until the landscape opened up into green hills the area is covered in fresh green ferns that look like a never ending landscape it was a hot morning as it got warmer i took off my outer sweater leaving me covered with my light spf windbreaker i was glad i had my sunglasses and cap i heard the high pitched chipmunk style music first and then i felt the funfair vibe i still have that atok ooo atok sound stuck in my head i saw many other people who were so determined to take photos with the green ferns even though the sun was intense i wanted to walk deeper into the ferns myself they look so bushy fresh and green but i was sweating and felt like my face skin was burning so i stayed back after taking photos we sat under a seller s big umbrella on portable chairs our guide mr kiki was very kind and bought us two skewers of aci cor with two different sauces he said he wanted us to experience the local foods i was moved by this i ve never had a guide buy food for me before and it really changed my perspective as it got warmer and we were running out of time we had to leave the fern garden further up was the teletubbies hills area i quietly regretted that we didn t manage to visit that specific spot but sitting in the shade eating and chatting with a great guide was still a highlight next time i come here i would like to find mr kiki again

one of the most beautiful places i have ever been to the view is breathtaking and the trek was challenging and exhausting we started our hike through sumber brantas you would need a health certificate from a government clinic to be able to climb not sure if they scrutimize it though as we were not this is transportation available from basecamp upto the base of the mountain which makes the climb easier the view on the way is also amazing from there on its climbclimbclimb there are three checkpoints until you reach the camp site the trek from up till is the most difficult and the journey would take up about hours from the base of the mountain the view near the camp ground is amazing and definitely worth the tiring climb from here you could climb summits arjuno which is to hours one way kembar and weiliriang that takes about in total back to camp and finally kembar there is not a lot of wildlife that you will come across other than some birds and wild boars that would come to camp at night in search of food there are also panthers that you might come across accoding to the rangers at basecamp our friends got a glimpse of one there have been no attacks at all and is not something to worry about its recommended that a minumum of people climb together unless you have a guide and a porter which can also be arranged at basecamp finally you need to carry a lot of water as it will be a to day affair and there are no close water sources near camp the nearest water source is and half hour away

this waterfall is a hour or so drive from the city of malang it seems to be in the middle of nowhere but there are many small shops and eateries warungs at the parkinglot next to the entrance so it isnt uninhabited here all toilets come with a charge even if you seem to be the customer of the place that owns the toilet to got to the waterfall is subject to an entrance fee after it you will walk on a concrete path to a viewpoint where you see the semicircular opening where the water comes down it is an impressive view and you can use two levels and a small plattform for taking pictures of people and the fall here you dont see the bottom of the fall after that you will have to go back a few steps to reach the place where the concrete path starts taking you down to the bottom of the fall most of this path is steep and only sometimes with something to hold on to there are sections with metal steps or metal grids to walk on and those are often more slippery than the concrete or the rocks you will have to walk through flowing water so your shoes need to agree with that there are small areas where you can take a rest and you will pass at least one section where drinks etc are sold at the bottom you will walk back and forth over log bridges that cross an active stream there will be mist coming towards you in this area that mist is similar to a light rain and it gets stronger the closer you get to the bottom of the fall here youll probably appreciate a rain cape if you have one you will need around minutes to get to the viewpoint and all the way down to the mist at the bottom and something similar to get back up to the parking lot another half an hour is enough for looking around at the bottom the viewpoint works for most visitors but going to the bottom is definitely not for everyone most people use shorts tshirt and sandals or flipflops for this visit there are people renting out shoes to those that dont have any there are cameras checking what happens on the trail down but please be careful if you go down
